title: Linux & Shell Basics
summary: Essential Linux commands and shell navigation for LLM work.

sections.beginner: Linux is the operating system most LLM training runs use. You do not need to be a Linux expert, but you should be comfortable navigating the filesystem, running commands, and managing processes.
sections.intermediate: Key skills: file management, process control, SSH, package management, environment variables, and basic scripting.
sections.advanced: Understanding systemd, cgroups, namespaces, and how Linux resource limits affect GPU training.
sections.deepdive: Kernel modules for NVIDIA drivers, GPU passthrough, and container runtime considerations.

title: Python Fundamentals
summary: Python is the primary language of LLM engineering.

sections.beginner: Variables, functions, control flow, data structures, and basic I/O. The foundation everything else builds on.
sections.intermediate: List comprehensions, generators, decorators, context managers, and OOP patterns used in ML codebases.
sections.advanced: Metaclasses, async/await, C extensions, and performance optimization techniques.
sections.deepdive: CPython internals, GIL behavior, and memory management in long-running training processes.

title: Git & Version Control
summary: Track changes, collaborate, and manage experiment code.

sections.advanced: Rebase workflows, cherry-picking, and managing large binary assets with Git LFS.
sections.deepdive: Git internals, object model, and how to recover from corruption in long training runs.

title: NumPy & Arrays
summary: Vectorized computation is the basis of all DL frameworks.

sections.advanced: Memory layout (C vs Fortran order), strided views, and performance characteristics of different operations.
sections.deepdive: NumPy's C backend, SIMD optimization, and how PyTorch tensors relate to NumPy arrays.

summary: Matrices, vectors, and operations that power every neural network.

sections.advanced: Kronecker products, tensor decompositions, and the linear algebra behind backpropagation.

title: Calculus for ML
summary: Derivatives and gradients are how models learn.

sections.intermediate: Jacobian and Hessian matrices, directional derivatives, and the chain rule applied to computation graphs.

title: Probability & Statistics
summary: Understanding uncertainty, distributions, and evaluation metrics.

sections.beginner: Random variables, probability distributions, expectation, variance, and Bayes' theorem. Foundation for understanding loss functions and sampling.
sections.intermediate: Maximum likelihood estimation, cross-entropy, KL divergence, and why they matter for language modeling.
sections.advanced: Concentration inequalities, statistical testing for evaluation, and confidence intervals for benchmarks.
sections.deepdive: Information theory basics: entropy, perplexity as an information-theoretic measure.

title: Optimization Fundamentals
summary: How gradient descent actually works.

sections.beginner: Loss landscapes, gradient descent, learning rate, and why optimization is harder than it looks.
sections.intermediate: Momentum, Adam, adaptive learning rates, and the difference between local and global minima in high dimensions.
sections.advanced: Saddle points, sparse gradients, saddle point escape strategies, and second-order methods.
sections.deepdive: Optimization theory: convergence rates, Lipschitz continuity, and why learning rate schedules matter more than optimizer choice.

title: Machine Learning Fundamentals
summary: From datasets to models: the ML workflow.

sections.beginner: Supervised vs unsupervised learning, training/validation/test splits, overfitting, regularization, and the bias-variance tradeoff.
sections.intermediate: Cross-validation, feature engineering, model selection, and basic evaluation metrics (accuracy, precision, recall).
sections.advanced: Regularization techniques, ensemble methods, and the statistical learning theory behind generalization.
sections.deepdive: Vapnik-Chervonenkis theory, Rademacher complexity, and why deep learning generalizes despite overparameterization.

summary: PyTorch tensors and automatic differentiation.

sections.intermediate: Computation graphs, backward passes, detached tensors, and in-place operations. Understanding what autograd actually tracks.
sections.advanced: Custom autograd functions, gradient accumulation, and memory-efficient backward passes.
sections.deepdive: PyTorch's autograd engine, Function classes, and how gradient checkpoints work at the engine level.

summary: From perceptrons to modern architectures.

sections.intermediate: Convolutional layers, pooling, batch normalization, initialization strategies, and training loops.
sections.advanced: Residual connections, layer normalization, and the design patterns that scale to deep networks.
sections.deepdive: Representational capacity, universal approximation theorem, and why depth matters more than width.

summary: Preventing overfitting: dropout, weight decay, and more.

summary: LayerNorm, RMSNorm, and why normalization is critical for transformers.

sections.beginner: Batch normalization in CNNs, layer normalization in transformers, and why they solve different problems.

summary: Stabilizing training by normalizing layer inputs.

title: Training Loops
summary: Building a correct training loop from scratch.

sections.beginner: Forward pass, loss computation, backward pass, optimizer step. The basic training loop pattern in PyTorch.
sections.intermediate: Gradient accumulation, mixed precision training, progress tracking, and validation loops.
sections.advanced: Gradient scaling for FP16, gradient clipping, and handling numerical instability in the training loop.
sections.deepdive: The exact order of operations in a training step, and common bugs that cause silent training failures.

summary: Saving and restoring training state safely.

sections.beginner: What to save (model weights, optimizer state, epoch, step), torch.save vs torch.save snapshot patterns.
sections.intermediate: Sharded checkpoints, FSDP checkpointing, ZeRO-3 save/load, and distributed checkpoint consistency.
sections.advanced: Checkpoint compression, incremental checkpointing, and recovery from partial failures.
sections.deepdive: Filesystem performance impact on checkpoint I/O, and strategies for managing checkpoint storage at scale.

title: Token Embeddings
summary: How words become vectors.

sections.beginner: Vocabulary, token IDs, embedding tables, and how lookups work. The simplest possible embedding layer.
sections.intermediate: Embedding dimension, vocabulary size trade-offs, and shared embeddings vs separate input/output embeddings.
sections.advanced: Soft prompts, prefix tuning, and how embeddings interact with tokenizer design.
sections.deepdive: Embedding table memory costs, quantization of embeddings, and the relationship between vocab size and training data.

summary: Giving the model a sense of token order.

summary: The position encoding used by LLaMA, Mistral, and most modern models.

title: Attention Mechanism
summary: The core innovation that made transformers possible.

sections.deepdive: Achieving O(n²) speedup through tiling and recomputation, and the trade-offs of approximate attention methods.

sections.beginner: Multiple attention heads in parallel, each learning different relationships. Concatenation and output projection.

sections.advanced: Multi-Query Attention (MQA), Grouped-Query Attention (GQA), and the compute-memory trade-off.

sections.advanced: Continuous batching, speculative decoding, and the trade-offs between latency and throughput in serving.
sections.deepdive: PagedAttention, vLLM architecture, and the cutting edge of inference optimization.

sections.beginner: During generation, we recompute attention over all previous tokens every step. KV cache stores previously computed K,V to avoid this.
sections.intermediate: Memory size of KV cache: 2 × seq_len × num_layers × num_kv_heads × head_dim × bytes_per_element. How it dominates memory for long contexts.
sections.advanced: PagedAttention (vLLM): treating KV cache like virtual memory. Slab allocation, page tables, and memory reuse.
sections.deepdive: Quantized KV cache, KV cache eviction policies, and the trade-offs between context length and throughput.

sections.beginner: Greedy decoding (always pick highest probability), temperature (control randomness), top-k (pick from top K), top-p (nucleus sampling).
sections.intermediate: Repetition penalty, presence penalty, frequency penalty, and combining sampling strategies for desired output style.
sections.advanced: Contrastive decoding, guided decoding, and constrained generation (JSON, schemas).
sections.deepdive: The physics of sampling: temperature as 'energy', the relationship between temperature and entropy, and empirical guidelines.

sections.beginner: MFU (Model FLOPs Utilization): how efficiently you're using your GPU's theoretical peak compute. Target: 40-60% for training.
sections.intermediate: Measuring MFU: theoretical FLOPs vs actual FLOPs. Throughput (tokens/sec/GPU), step time breakdown, and bottleneck identification.
sections.advanced: Achieving high MFU: kernel fusion, communication overlap, memory bandwidth utilization, and hardware-aware scheduling.
sections.deepdive: The MFU vs GFLOPs discussion, why peak FLOPs is rarely achievable, and the gap between theoretical and practical throughput.

sections.beginner: torch.profiler, TensorBoard, wandb. How to measure step time, GPU utilization, and memory usage during training.
sections.intermediate: Flame graphs, CUDA event timing, and identifying CPU bottlenecks vs GPU bottlenecks.
sections.advanced: nsys profiling, NCCL debug tools, and deep performance analysis for distributed training.
sections.deepdive: Root cause analysis of training slowdowns, and the systematic approach to performance debugging at scale.

sections.beginner: From trained model to serving API. Model serialization, inference engines (vLLM, TGI), and basic deployment patterns.
sections.intermediate: Containerization, autoscaling, model versioning, and the operational concerns of serving LLMs in production.
sections.advanced: Multi-model serving, A/B testing, canary deployments, and the monitoring stack for LLM services.
sections.deepdive: Production latency optimization, GPU utilization in serving, and the economics of inference deployment at scale.
